question: Can already-produced DSpark hidden rows predict enough authoritative K3 Budget24 slab misses early enough to hide at least 0.20 seconds of V8 expert delivery under exact Core8?
hypothesis: Applying each existing layer-specific target Router8 to the seven DSpark proposal hidden rows will recall at least half of the physical miss bytes later requested by authoritative routing, without changing target semantics.
borrow_first: existing immutable per-layer Router8 graphs and weights
existing P20/P30 I/O trace and cache-oracle script
capture: proxy and authoritative top-16 expert IDs and weights
authoritative aligned record keys and explicit physical miss bytes
primary_metrics: net service wall after false-prefetch and proxy-router cost
correctness_contract: authoritative Router8 remains the sole route and weight authority
a prefetched record may be consumed only after exact layer/offset/length match
every missing authoritative record is read synchronously
wrong predictions never enter P30 or P40 and are discarded
target IDs, logits, recurrent and MLA state, logical traffic, and canonical joins remain unchanged
abort_conditions: gross physical-miss byte recall below 37.53 percent
capture requires a new scheduler, cache, queue, or benchmark framework
proxy computation mutates authoritative target state
any fixture misses the frozen GO thresholds

interpretation.GO: Implement the smallest existing-queue prefetch seam and run same-binary reversed exact A/B.
interpretation.NO_GO: Delete capture code and close DSpark-hidden pre-route prediction at V8 under the current draft and Budget24 representation.
interpretation.INVALID: Fix only the recorded capture/measurement defect; do not widen gates.
